beats.title: Edwin Smith Papyrus Describes Exams
beats.description: An Egyptian medical text sets out a step-by-step routine of looking at, feeling and judging injuries before treating them.

beats.title: Hippocratic Bedside Diagnosis
beats.description: Greek physicians of the Hippocratic school taught doctors to read a patient's body, pulse, skin and breathing to judge illness.

beats.title: Herophilus Studies the Pulse
beats.description: An Alexandrian physician timed the pulse against a water clock and linked its rhythm to health and disease.

beats.title: Wang Shuhe's Pulse Classic
beats.description: A Chinese physician compiled a classic text that sorted the pulse into many distinct types, each read as a sign of illness.

beats.title: Avicenna's Canon Codifies Diagnosis
beats.description: A Persian scholar's encyclopedia described pulse-taking, urine inspection and careful examination as the basis of diagnosis.

beats.title: Vesalius Publishes Human Anatomy
beats.description: A richly illustrated book, based on human dissection, corrected centuries of error about what lies inside the body.

beats.title: Santorio Takes a Body Temperature
beats.description: An Italian physician put a thermoscope in a patient's mouth to measure fever, an early try at quantifying body heat.

beats.title: Leeuwenhoek Sees Blood Cells
beats.description: A Dutch cloth merchant with homemade lenses was the first to describe red blood cells under a microscope.

beats.title: Floyer's Pulse-Watch
beats.description: An English physician had a watch made that ran for exactly one minute, so a doctor could count the pulse rate.

beats.title: Auenbrugger Taps the Chest
beats.description: A Viennese doctor published a method of tapping the chest and listening to the sound to detect fluid and disease.

beats.title: Bozzini's Light Conductor
beats.description: A German physician used candlelight reflected down a tube to peer into body cavities, the forerunner of the endoscope.

beats.title: Laennec Invents the Stethoscope
beats.description: A French doctor rolled up a sheet of paper to listen to a patient's heart and later made a wooden tube for the job.

beats.title: Helmholtz's Ophthalmoscope
beats.description: A German scientist built a device that lets a doctor look through the pupil at the living back of the eye.

beats.title: Garcia Views His Own Larynx
beats.description: A singing teacher used mirrors and sunlight to watch his own vocal cords at work, founding the laryngoscope.

beats.title: Allbutt's Pocket Thermometer
beats.description: A British physician introduced a short thermometer that read a patient's temperature in minutes rather than a quarter hour.

beats.title: Nitze Builds the Cystoscope
beats.description: A German urologist showed a lit telescope-like tube that could be passed into the bladder to inspect it.

beats.title: Basch's Blood Pressure Meter
beats.description: An Austrian physician devised the first practical device to measure blood pressure without cutting into an artery.

beats.title: Koch Identifies the TB Germ
beats.description: A German physician stained and grew the bacterium behind tuberculosis, making lab diagnosis of the disease possible.

beats.title: Riva-Rocci's Blood Pressure Cuff
beats.description: An Italian doctor wrapped an inflatable cuff around the upper arm, giving a simple, reliable way to read blood pressure.

beats.title: Landsteiner Discovers Blood Groups
beats.description: An Austrian scientist found that human blood falls into distinct types, which made testing and safe transfusion possible.

beats.title: Einthoven Builds the ECG Machine
beats.description: A Dutch physiologist used a sensitive string galvanometer to record the heart's electrical activity from the skin.

beats.title: Wassermann Test for Syphilis
beats.description: A German bacteriologist introduced a blood test that could detect syphilis infection before symptoms revealed it.

beats.title: Salomon Maps Tumours by Mammogram
beats.description: A German surgeon X-rayed removed breasts and showed how tumours looked, the start of breast imaging.

beats.title: Berger Records the Brain's Waves
beats.description: A German psychiatrist attached electrodes to a human scalp and recorded the brain's electrical rhythms for the first time.

beats.title: Papanicolaou's Smear Test
beats.description: A Greek-American scientist showed that cells taken from the cervix could reveal cancer before symptoms appeared.

beats.title: Forssmann Catheterises His Heart
beats.description: A young German doctor pushed a tube through a vein in his own arm all the way into his heart, then walked to get an X-ray.

beats.title: Dussik Scans the Brain with Sound
beats.description: An Austrian neurologist passed sound waves through a patient's head to try to picture the inside of the skull.

beats.title: Apgar Scores Newborns
beats.description: An American anaesthesiologist devised a quick five-point check of a baby's health in the first minutes after birth.

beats.title: Fibre-Optic Endoscope Debuts
beats.description: A flexible bundle of glass fibres carried light so doctors could view the inside of a living patient's stomach.

beats.title: Ultrasound Scans a Pregnancy
beats.description: A Glasgow obstetrician published images made with sound waves of a growing baby in the womb.

beats.title: First CT Scan of a Patient
beats.description: A London hospital used a rotating X-ray machine and a computer to image a woman's brain slice by slice.

beats.title: First Home Pregnancy Test
beats.description: A boxed kit with test tube and chemicals let women check for pregnancy in private rather than at a doctor's office.

beats.title: First MRI Scan of a Human
beats.description: A huge magnet and radio waves produced an image of a man's chest without any radiation.

beats.title: First HIV Blood Test
beats.description: Blood banks began screening donations with an antibody test for the virus that causes AIDS.

beats.title: fMRI Watches the Working Brain
beats.description: Researchers used magnetic scanning to show blood flow changes in a living human brain as it responded to tasks.

beats.title: Swallowable Camera Pill Is Unveiled
beats.description: A pill-sized camera that patients swallow was reported to film the whole digestive tract as it passed through.

beats.title: Smartwatch Takes an ECG
beats.description: A wrist-worn consumer watch gained approval to record a heart tracing and flag an irregular rhythm.

beats.title: Mass Testing for a New Coronavirus
beats.description: Swab tests and rapid kits were used by millions to check for infection with a newly emerged virus.
